### Contract review brief — PR #37937 @ `7eb79ca63cc00a4dd786cb9805ae911d13f7ea94` (card #37857)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #37857: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #37937: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `7eb79ca63cc00a4dd786cb9805ae911d13f7ea94`
  · the check-runs on `7eb79ca63cc00a4dd786cb9805ae911d13f7ea94`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — a `hits` path sits on the low-risk skills arm: when the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `SCRATCHPAD/pr-37937/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7eb79ca63cc00a4dd786cb9805ae911d13f7ea94`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json + scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs
Security-touching: no

Read for this record: card #37857 (body and its two comments, the claim 7217200370 and the os-dev-report 7217889058), PR #37937 (body, four-file list, net diff against `main`, merge base `73d5e347`), and the check-runs on the head. Cited code was read on `main` at `f926dfab`.

Check-runs on `7eb79ca6` as read (47 runs): 24 success, 18 skipped, 5 still running at the last read (7 at the first). Success, by name, among them the lanes that carry this diff's own gates: `Type Check · source gates` (holds `check-skills-token-ratchet` and its self-test, and `check:skill-links`), `Lint · docs & code guards` (holds `check:skill-identifier-liveness`), `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)`, `Build Core`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Test Core (3/10)`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Auto Label`, `filter`. **Still `in_progress`, no conclusion read:** `Test Core (1/10)`, `Test Core (2/10)`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`. No run has failed. The verdict below is on the design; the five running lanes are the adopting seat's to read to green before this record carries the PR anywhere.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Published skill text, `objectstack-ai`: one subsection out, one sentence in. Right.** The subsection *The Ask AI button* and its `os:check` `defineAction` example leave; nothing else in the file linked to it (no other line of `skills/objectstack-ai/**` names the heading, the type or the example). The accept-set of the spec is not touched by this diff: `ActionType` on `main` (`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts:706`) still holds the member, and its removal is #37856 / PR #37924.
- **Eval case 10: same id, same prompt, opposite expected answer. Right.** The reader takes ids as given, so cases 11 and 12 keep their numbers. The case still asserts something (`cases.ts` refuses a case with neither list), and the grader is a literal, case-sensitive substring match (`packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/grade.ts`), against which the reference answer passes and the old answer fails on all three tokens.
- **Token ceiling 6799 to 6617, lowered only. Right.** By the script's own audit rule, `ceil((bytes - stamp line) / 4)`: the head's file is 26493 bytes, its stamp line (`  version: "19.0.0-next.0"`) 27, giving 6617; `main`'s is 27222 bytes, giving 6799. The lane that runs the ratchet is green on the head.
- **`skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md` lines 151 and 153 stay. Right for this head.** `scripts/check-skill-identifier-liveness.mjs:388` registers the *Action Types* table as exhaustive over `ActionType`; with the member still on `main`, deleting the row is a `[leg2-missing-row]` failure, and the gap ledger is the maintainer's. So the card's acceptance, an empty `git grep -n ask_ai -- skills/`, is not met by this PR: the grep prints exactly those two lines on the head. `Part of #37857` is the correct relation and the card must stay open.
- **Nothing else under `skills/**` on `main` teaches an authored AI button.** `git grep ask_ai -- skills/` on `main` names three files; this PR clears two. Greps for `Ask AI`, `ai:chat`, `chatbot` and `in-app assistant` under `skills/` find no further teaching of a page AI button (the `ai:chat` menu entry is named only in a generated reference index and is a navigation entry, which D6 does not retire).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/skills` `patch` is right: the package exists under that name (`packages/skills/package.json`), `skills/**` is what it ships, and the diff changes published prose and one eval case, no key, value or type an author can write. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right for the same reason: what an author can write changes in PR #37924, not here. `Clause-②: no` stands, on the PR body and in the changeset, with no arm. No BREAKING banner is owed: nothing is removed from any accept-set by this diff.

Clause-②: no

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question, who deletes the two `objectstack-ui` lines: answer A.** The row is bound by a gate to the enum member, so it leaves in the diff that removes the member (PR #37924), with the `objectstack-ui` token row following its measurement there. The sentence under the table (`Every type but script and ask_ai requires target`) goes with it. This card then closes on a re-read that the grep is empty. Not C: no reason here justifies a ledgered gap. The choice is the seat's to record on the card; this record only says A is consistent with the gate and the ADR.
- **Deviation, `Part of` in place of `Fixes`:** correct, see ①.
- **Deviation, two files outside the claimed `skills/**` surface:** both forced. The ratchet's row must follow the measurement down in the PR that shrinks the file, and a diff that publishes owes a changeset. Neither is under `packages/**` or `docs/adr/**`. The ratchet script is reviewed in ④ as the enforcing file; the changeset is the lane seat's ACCEPT.
- **Deviation, landing order reversed against the claim comment:** the reason given (the `os:check` example stops type-checking once the member leaves) agrees with the tree: the example on `main` writes `type: 'ask_ai'` through `defineAction`. The claim comment's "lands after C1" line is stale and is the seat's to correct on the card.
- **Interim state on `main` between the two merges:** `objectstack-ai` says no page declares an AI button while `objectstack-ui` still lists the type and the spec still parses it. Accepted as a deviation on one condition the seat owns: no release of `@objectstack/skills`, a `next` prerelease included, is cut between this merge and PR #37924's. If one could be, the two PRs should merge back to back.
- **Remaining deviations** (no assignee, maintainer-summary form, worktree left in place, commit trailers) are process matters for the seat; none touches the contract.
- **Out-of-scope finding, the English label:** see N1 below; its carrier is #37858, as the dev says.
- **SQL push-down:** not applicable. The diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no join.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`.** The replacement sentence, read against ADR-0160 on `main` (seventh amendment):

- "No page declares an AI button of its own" is D6 "Entry point" word for word, and point 7 of the summary ("No page has an AI button of its own").
- "so there is no action to write for one" follows from D7 (the type is retired; a legacy action is refused where metadata is authored). The sentence does not say the parse refuses anything, which is correct on this head: on `main` the type still parses, and the refusal is PR #37924's to build and word. It teaches nothing that is false on `main` and nothing #37924 has yet to deliver.
- "the shell's 「问 AI」 entry opens the in-app assistant" is D6's name for the entry and D7's own prescription text ("use the shell's 「问 AI」 entry").
- "and carries the current record automatically" is the card's own wording (step 2) and holds on `main` in the sense the same file already teaches at its *In-app `ask` assistant* paragraph: the client sends `recordId` with the turn. The stronger reading, D6's default focus, is #37861's and not yet built; the sentence does not claim it. It is unqualified where D6 is qualified (a list or dashboard has no record; a sent conversation keeps its own), which is acceptable for one sentence whose job is to stop an authored action.
- Placement: last paragraph of *Actions as AI Tools — the default path ☁️*, the section an author reads when asked to "write the action". The section's cloud mark covers it, and D6 agrees that the open edition shows no AI button.
- I tried to break it against the prompt: an author told to add an AI button to a record page now finds, in the section on actions, that there is none to write and what the user does instead. With `objectstack-ui` loaded beside it the table row still offers the type until PR #37924; that is the interim state in ③, not a defect of this file.

No changed hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour. The removed text spoke of tool exposure (`ai.exposed`, `run_action`) only to say the retired type had none; the added sentence speaks of no access rule. Hence `Security-touching: no`.

**`skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json`, case 10.** The expected answer agrees with D6 and D7 and with the sentence above. `must_contain: ["问 AI"]` matches the skill's and the ADR's spelling byte for byte. `must_not_contain: ["defineAction(", "locations:"]` catches the answer the old skill taught and an action embedded under an object's `actions` that declares `locations`. The type's own literal is unavailable as a forbidden token, since the card's acceptance wants that string out of `skills/`. The case discriminates the pair it exists for.

**`scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`** (enforcing file). One row, lowered, to the measured value; the added comment states the cause correctly. The row's trailing comment (`-18 (was 6824), then -5 ...`) predates this PR and is left as it was.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):

- N1 (nit) — the skill is English prose and names the entry only as 「问 AI」. That is the ADR's name, but on `main` the label is per locale: `Ask AI` in `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts`, `问 AI` in `zh-Hans.ts`, `AI に質問` in `ja.ts`. An English-locale author will not see the string the skill gives. Leave it here; #37858 owns what the button reads, and the skill can follow that card.
- N2 (nit) — case 10's forbidden tokens miss an action written as JSON (`"locations": [` does not contain `locations:`), the form `objectstack-ui` uses in its own examples, and an action written with no `locations` key. Such an answer still fails unless it also names the entry, so the hole is an answer that names the entry and writes the action anyway. Adding `record_header` to `must_not_contain` would close most of it; the reference answer does not spell it.
- N3 (nit) — `must_contain` is one CJK token with an inner space and the grader normalises nothing, so a correct answer that writes `问AI` (the maintainer's own spelling in the rulings) or `Ask AI` fails. Accepted: the skill under test spells it exactly as the token does.

Conditions on adopting this PASS, none of them a finding on the diff: the five running check-runs named above conclude green on this head; the card stays open for the two `objectstack-ui` lines; the release condition in ③ holds.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-q0nzop`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibvMMgnKA797JY46H9i`

**VERDICT: PASS**

### Checklist

- **Shape and relation.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Part of #37857`. No closing keyword anywhere in the body (`l1-face` keyword scan clean). `Part of` is correct. The card's acceptance (`git grep -n ask_ai -- skills/` empty) is not met on this head: `skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md:151/:153` remain. `scripts/check-skill-identifier-liveness.mjs:388` binds that table to `ActionType`, and `ActionType` still holds the member on `main`. #37857 keeps `pm:dispatched` for its second half (landing rule B). Route B was recorded on the card in claim amendment 7218076053.
- **Scope.** Four files. The ratchet row and the changeset lie outside the original `skills/**` surface. Each is forced by a gate, and the claim amendment 7218076053 now names both. No other file is in the diff.
- **Changeset, read sentence by sentence** (`.changeset/37857-skill-no-authored-ai-button.md`). `@objectstack/skills` is a published package (`packages/skills/package.json`: not private, `files` ships `dist`). `patch` is correct for prose plus one eval case. Each body sentence is true at this head:
  - the D6 quote;
  - the subsection's removal and the one-sentence replacement, matching the `SKILL.md` hunk byte for byte in meaning;
  - the ceiling 6799 to 6617, matching the ratchet row;
  - case 10's prompt kept, with `must_contain` `问 AI` and `must_not_contain` `defineAction(` and `locations:`, matching the eval hunk;
  - the `objectstack-ui` table left unchanged, matching the diff.
- **Test and gate evidence.** The os-dev-report (7217889058) pins its readings to `7eb79ca6`, the current head. The eval carries a positive control and a negative control. The reference answer passes its grader. An answer that writes the action fails on all three tokens. The ratchet shows red before the row moved and green after. Check-runs at this head: 31 success, 18 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending. Lint & Repo Gates: success. TypeScript Type Check: success. No dogfood battery is owed (no `!` in the title, no narrowing arm).
- **Value density (`skills/**`, read from a customer agent that loads the whole package).** A 25-line subsection and an example that taught a type now being retired are replaced by one sentence. That sentence sends the agent to the shell entry. The file goes 6799 to 6617 tokens. The whole shipped tree goes 301286 to 301061 tokens.
- **The replacement sentence is true on `main`.** It does not claim that the parse refuses `ask_ai`. That refusal is #37924's job. L2 ④ checked the sentence against ADR-0160 D6/D7.

### Accepted deviations

- L2 nits N1–N3 (comment 7218046640) are accepted without a head move:
  - **N1.** The en bundle says `Ask AI` today, while the skill says 「问 AI」. What the button reads belongs to #37858. Its PR #37885 pins 「问 AI」 in `AssistantTopBarButton.askAi-37858.test.tsx`.
  - **N2 and N3.** These are eval-token tightness only.
- The os-dev-report lists `status: "rework"`, but its content is a complete hand-back. The one open question was answered by the seat on the card (B).
- The PR has no assignee, per the dispatch order. The seat's hand-off assigns it.

### Landing condition (carried from L2 ③)

No `@objectstack/skills` release, a `next` prerelease included, may be cut between this PR's merge and #37924's. This PR lands first.
